title: NaOCl in the canal: why refresh it?
topic: How tissue reactions use up NaOCl's hydroxide and free chlorine (saponification, neutralization, chloramination), so it must be refreshed.

claims.claim: Assumed: unbuffered NaOCl, 2.5–6%, pH ~11–12, pulp remnants, no agitation
claims.source: pH ~11–12: Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz, Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 3:588-612 (PMID 35338652); van der Waal et al., Quintessence Int 2014;45:467-74 (PMID 24701613; mean pH 11.5 in practice solutions). 2.5–6% is a stated assumption within the 0.5–8.25% range of proposed concentrations (Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz 2022)
Estrela et al., Braz Dent J 2002;13(2):113-7 (PMID 12238801)

claims.claim: At pH 11–12 this lies far left: free chlorine is mostly OCl⁻
claims.source: Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz, Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 3:588-612 (PMID 35338652); HOCl pKa ~7.5 (standard chemistry)

claims.claim: Saponification: fat + NaOH → soap + glycerol (uses OH⁻)
claims.source: Estrela et al., Braz Dent J 2002;13(2):113-7 (PMID 12238801); reaction drawing is schematic

claims.claim: Neutralization: amino acid + NaOH → salt + H₂O (uses OH⁻, so pH falls)
claims.source: Estrela et al., Braz Dent J 2002;13(2):113-7 (PMID 12238801); reaction drawing is schematic

claims.claim: Chloramination: R–NH₂ + HOCl → R–NHCl + H₂O (uses free chlorine); HOCl/OCl⁻ also oxidize and break down proteins
claims.source: Estrela et al., Braz Dent J 2002;13(2):113-7 (PMID 12238801)

claims.claim: Free chlorine near tissue gets used up when left alone; refreshing puts it back (sawtooth graph)
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: unit-free, time & amounts illustrative, two separate runs; the ~90% partial reset is a modelling choice. Consumption: Moorer & Wesselink, Int Endod J 1982;15:187-96 (PMID 6964523); Tejada et al., Int Endod J 2019;52:114-122 (PMID 30019752); frequent exchange: Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz 2022 (PMID 35338652)

claims.claim: Tissue & dentin use it up → refresh often
claims.source: Macedo et al., Int Endod J 2010;43:1108-15 (PMID 20812947); Tejada et al., Int Endod J 2019;52:114-122 (PMID 30019752); Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz, Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 3:588-612 (PMID 35338652); Cullen et al., J Endod 2015;41:920-4 (PMID 25791075)

caption:
Why does NaOCl in a canal need to be refreshed?
Unbuffered NaOCl (pH ~11–12) dissolves pulp tissue by reacting with it, and those reactions use it up.
Saponification and amino-acid neutralization consume hydroxide; chloramination and oxidation consume free chlorine (HOCl + OCl⁻).
Tissue and dentin deplete free chlorine at the interface, so exchange it often. Agitation and concentration matter too.
Refs: Estrela 2002, Braz Dent J; Moorer & Wesselink 1982, Int Endod J; Tejada 2019, Int Endod J; Boutsioukis & Arias-Moliz 2022, Int Endod J; Stojicic 2010, J Endod
Animation is schematic; graph is a toy model.
